description: Per-release compatibility and migration guidance for the Charter specification, schemas, conformance corpus, and Go reference SDK. Newest first. README.md documents the current state; this file is the versioned history GOVERNANCE.md requires of every release.

field_notes.version: semantic version of the repository release and Go module tag (v<version>); the body identifies the supported specification and schema versions

migrations.title: Stored documents, account links, and binding packages
migrations.summary: Adds a tenant-scoped document store, keel account links, binding-package manifests and materialization, and pre-activation readiness. The new package format raises the schema catalogue to 2.3.0; Charter documents and the 1.2.0 specification are unchanged. Updates the optional keel adapter to keel v1.2.86.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Versions

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.2.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`) | 2.3.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.2.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.2.2 |
| Optional keel adapter (`sdk/adapter/keel`) | keel v1.2.86 |

## Compatibility impact

Additive. Charter document schemas, fixtures, rules, and conformance claims are unchanged. The catalogue adds the binding-package manifest format. keel v1.2.76 to v1.2.86 are additive for the adapter's surface (`common`, `guard`, `idempotency`, `model`, `port`).

## Go SDK — new

| Symbol | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `corpus.DefinitionVersion` | The version a versioned definition kind declares: `definitionVersion`, `processDefinitionVersion`, `taskDefinitionVersion`, `contractVersion`, or a binding's `bindingVersion`. |
| `validate.Additions` | `Validate(ctx, source, docs...)` checks documents before a store commits them: structure, the catalog's specification version, and references resolved against a `corpus.Source`. Only the referenced documents are fetched, so the cost follows the write, not the store; a source read failure is an error, never a finding. |
| `binding.PackageManifest`, `binding.ParsePackageManifest`, `binding.Materialize` | Defines a portable contract realization with binding templates, adapter and observer references, a parameter schema, feature and lossy-mapping declarations, and conformance cases; materialization validates parameters and emits customer-namespaced binding documents. |
| `capability.BaseInvoker.Readiness`, `capability.Blocker` | Reports, before a binding goes live, every denial that follows from documents and composition: contract, capability binding and declared features, an authority binding for the profile, and the approval gate, SoD checker, ledger, and effect observer the contract requires. |
| `keel.DocumentStore` | A `corpus.Source` per tenant over `charter_document` and append-only `charter_document_revision`. `Save` validates, commits a batch atomically, replays identical content, and refuses evidence kinds (`ErrEvidenceDocument`), kind changes (`ErrKindChanged`), enterprise changes (`ErrEnterpriseChanged`), and different content under a stored definition version (`ErrPublishedVersion`); validation failures are `*InvalidDocumentsError` wrapping `ErrInvalidDocument`. |
| `keel.HumanAccounts`, `keel.HumanAccount` | `charter_human_account` links from a keel `partner_user` membership to a stored `HumanIdentity` for a half-open period; links stay within their membership and never overlap per human or per user. |
| `keel.TableIdentityMap` | An `IdentityMap` that resolves a human session's keel user through the effective link, so tokens need no Charter claims; agents keep `BaseClaimIdentityMap`. The user is the `keel_user_id` claim or else the `user:<id>` subject (`KeelUserSubjectPrefix`) keel's authorization server mints. |

## Keel schema module

`sdk/adapter/keel/schema/` holds two groups: `charter_document` (`document/`, depends on keel `tenant_management`) and `charter_identity` (`identity/`, depends on `charter_document`). Pass the groups in use to keel's `schemagen -input` after keel's `core`, `geo`, and `tenant_management`.

## Adoption

1. `go get github.com/nauticana/charter@v1.2.2`; with `sdk/adapter/keel`, keel v1.2.86.
2. A downstream that kept Charter documents or human-to-user links in its own tables can generate the module's tables, load its documents through `DocumentStore.Save`, and compose `TableIdentityMap` in place of its own identity map.
3. Parse the selected package manifest, call `binding.Materialize` with the customer profile and parameters, and validate or save the resulting documents.
4. Call `Readiness` on the composed invoker before activating a binding.

migrations.title: Keel 1.2.75 compatibility
migrations.summary: Updates the optional Keel adapter from keel v1.2.68 to v1.2.75. No adapter source changes. The Charter specification, schema catalogue, conformance profiles, and document formats are unchanged from 1.2.0.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Versions

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.2.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`) | 2.2.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.2.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.2.1 |
| Optional keel adapter (`sdk/adapter/keel`) | keel v1.2.75 |

## Compatibility impact

None. keel v1.2.69 to v1.2.75 are additive for the adapter's surface (`common`, `guard`, `idempotency`, `model`, `port`); only the module requirement changes. keel's breaking changes in that range (`client.CredentialStore.UpsertConnection`, the `/inbox` → `/notifications` routes, `payment.ChargeAuthenticationRequired`) are outside what the adapter imports.

## Adoption

1. `go get github.com/nauticana/charter@v1.2.1`; with `sdk/adapter/keel`, keel v1.2.75.
2. Run the downstream test suite. No Charter documents, schemas, fixtures, or conformance claims require migration.

migrations.title: Verified capability effects and reconciliation of unknown outcomes
migrations.summary: A mutating capability can declare verifiable postconditions, and an action is executed only once their observed state says so; an unknown outcome is reconciled from observation alone by a new record naming the attempt, never by re-execution. Adds CHR-CAP-009, CHR-CAP-010, CHR-EVID-011, CHR-EVID-012, four active rules, and optional schema members. Specification 1.2.0, schema catalogue 2.2.0; every document declares the new specification version and is otherwise unchanged. SDK source breaks: AbstractInvoker is BaseInvoker and validate.Subject.Compose takes the scripted External system. The optional adapter targets keel v1.2.68.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Versions

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.2.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`) | 2.2.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.2.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.2.0 |
| Optional keel adapter (`sdk/adapter/keel`) | keel v1.2.68 |

## Why

The specification required declared outcomes and categorized evidence, but nothing tied an `executed` disposition to the state of the external system. A provider can accept a mutation and still hold the old value; recording that as executed is false. Separately, `CHR-RULE-RT-003` blocked a retry after an unknown outcome without saying what evidence may resolve it.

## New requirements

| Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CHR-CAP-009` | A mutating capability may declare postconditions: stable id, statement, the outcomes it applies to, whether it must be verified, and optionally the declared business error a violation is recorded as. |
| `CHR-CAP-010` | No `executed` while a verification-required postcondition applying to the outcome is violated or unknown. Violated is failed (or the mapped business error); an observation failure after submission is unknown. An absent effect is retried under the same key only when the contract declares it safe. |
| `CHR-EVID-011` | A postcondition evaluation is satisfied, violated, or unknown, with observation time and reason; satisfied and violated reference observed-fact records. The external response and the observed state stay distinct records; an acknowledgement is not effect evidence. |
| `CHR-EVID-012` | An unknown mutating outcome is reconciled only through a new observation. Established effects append an executed record naming the attempt it reconciles, without submitting the operation again; otherwise the outcome stays unknown. The original record is never restated. |

## Schema — additive, all new members optional

| Kind | New member |
|---|---|
| `CapabilityContract` | `postconditions[]` (`id`, `statement`, `verificationRequired`, `outcomes`, `violationBusinessError`), allowed only when `idempotency.mutating` is true; `idempotency.retryWhenEffectAbsent` |
| `ActionRecord` | `postconditionEvaluations[]` (`postconditionId`, `result`, `reason`, `observedAt`, `evidenceRecordIds`); `reconcilesActionId`, which requires `postconditionEvaluations` |
| `EvidenceRecord` | `integrity`, whose value digests the `content` member so one record is verifiable outside a bundle |
| `common.schema.json` | `$defs/integrity`, now shared by `EvidenceBundle` and `EvidenceRecord` |
| fixture descriptor | `reconcile` and `observation` on a step; `observer_calls`, `postconditions`, `reconciled` on `expect` |

Every document must declare `"charterSpecVersion": "1.2.0"`; one that declares no postconditions is otherwise unchanged, and no existing kind, rule, or requirement changed meaning.

## Conformance

| Rule | Profile | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| `CHR-RULE-CAP-002` | core-model | postconditions stay within their contract; evaluations belong to it and rest on observed facts; `executed` has every required postcondition satisfied |
| `CHR-RULE-EVID-002` | core-model | a reconciling record names an unknown attempt of the same actor and capability that does not follow it |
| `CHR-RULE-RT-009` | agent-runtime | accepted and observed → executed; accepted but unchanged → failed; accepted but unobservable or unevidenced → unknown; never a second mutation |
| `CHR-RULE-RT-010` | agent-runtime | reconciliation observes without calling the transport, appends the reconciling record, and a replay returns it; an unobservable attempt stays unknown and the blind retry is refused |

The core-model profile lists 26 rules and agent-runtime 10. The Harbor reservation contract now declares the verification-required postcondition `POST-RESERVATION-HELD`, so every runtime fixture that expects `executed` for it scripts an `observation`; Harbor records the timed-out attempt and its reconciliation as two action records. Conformance claims regenerate against the 1.2.0 manifest; re-run `charter claim` for each active profile.

## Go SDK — breaking

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `capability.AbstractInvoker` | `capability.BaseInvoker` — it is complete and usable as composed |
| `validate.Subject.Compose(ctx, documents, transport binding.Executor)` | `Compose(ctx, documents, external validate.External)`; compose `external.Transport` and `external.Observer` |
| `validate.Runtime{Admission, Invoker, Evidence}` | adds `Reconciler capability.Reconciler`; reconcile steps fail against a runtime that exposes none |

## Go SDK — new

- `binding.Observer`, `ObservationRequest`, `Observation`: the read-only boundary that evaluates postconditions against the external state and names the declared outcome that state corresponds to. It records what it saw as observed-fact evidence and returns the references.
- `BaseInvoker.Observer`. A mutating contract with a verification-required postcondition is denied before the transport when no observer is composed. After an accepted mutation the invoker downgrades to unknown any evaluation that is missing, unrecognized, or reported without evidence.
- `capability.Reconciler`, `capability.Reconciliation`, `BaseInvoker.Reconcile`: re-runs the gates, proves the ledger fence with `MarkUnknown` before observing, never calls the transport, and completes, fails, or leaves the key unknown. A violated effect completes the key as failed, or releases it when `retryWhenEffectAbsent` is set.
- `capability.Result.Postconditions`; `model.Postcondition`, `model.PostconditionEvaluation`, `CapabilityContract.RequiredPostconditions`, `ActionRecord.PostconditionEvaluations`, `ActionRecord.ReconcilesActionID`, `EvidenceRecord.Integrity`, `Idempotency.RetryWhenEffectAbsent`.
- `evidence.Seal` and `evidence.Verifier.VerifyRecord` for the content digest of one record.
- `validate.VerifiedEffectRule`, `validate.ReconciliationRule`.

## Keel 1.2.68

keel v1.2.65 to v1.2.68 are additive for the adapter's surface (`common`, `guard`, `idempotency`, `model`, `port`); only the module requirement changes. `BaseInvoker.Reconcile` relies on `MarkUnknown` being idempotent for the fence holder, which keel's memory and pgsql ledgers are.

## Adoption

1. `go get github.com/nauticana/charter@v1.2.0`; with `sdk/adapter/keel`, keel v1.2.68. Set `charterSpecVersion` to `1.2.0` in every document and `specification_version` in every fixture descriptor.
2. Rename `AbstractInvoker` to `BaseInvoker`.
3. A `validate.Subject` takes `External` in `Compose`, wires both of its members, and returns a `Reconciler`.
4. For each mutating capability whose effect can be read back, declare postconditions and implement `binding.Observer` in the adapter that owns the external system. Persist `Result.LedgerFence` and the action id of an unknown attempt so it can be presented to `Reconcile`.
5. Replace reconciliation that rewrote or retried an unknown attempt with `Reconcile`; it appends a new record and leaves the first as written.

migrations.title: Mediation of governed acts
migrations.summary: Adds the CHR-MED area: a protocol-neutral model for a governed act submitted to another party for a decision before it takes effect, with the MediationProfile and MediationDecision kinds, four active core-model rules, and typed SDK structs. Specification 1.1.0, schema catalogue 2.1.0. No existing document, rule, or requirement changed meaning; every document declares the new specification version.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Additive — a new normative area, `CHR-MED`

Charter gains a thirteenth chapter, [Mediation of Governed Acts](spec/13_mediation.md), for the case where a governed act is submitted to another party for a decision before it takes effect. Platforms that host agents increasingly offer such a callout, and until now Charter could evidence an act that was authorized but not a decision that prevented one.

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.1.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`) | 2.1.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.1.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.1.0 |

### What is new

- **Eleven requirements, `CHR-MED-001` to `CHR-MED-011`.** A mediation point declares its stage, outcomes, failure policy, decision budget, coverage, and evidence. A decision is reached before the act takes effect, identifies its subject, names a declared outcome, carries a subject reason and an audit reference when it is not an allow, and is never recorded as an allow when the mediator produced nothing.
- **Alignment with existing runtime-governance specifications.** The outcome vocabulary is the five dispositions of the OWASP Agent Control Standard; obligations may accompany any outcome, including decision-handling duties after denial, as in the OpenID AuthZEN obligations model; common stages cover model, tool, retrieval, memory, session, and turn hooks while bindings can name additional hooks; and a profile declares an `enforcementMode` of `enforce` or `shadow`, the dry-run pattern of admission webhooks, with each decision recording whether it was `enforced` and distinguishing applied from proposed obligations.
- **Two document kinds**, `MediationProfile` and `MediationDecision`, in `schema/mediation/`.
- **Four active core-model rules**, `CHR-RULE-MED-001` to `CHR-RULE-MED-004`, with valid and invalid fixtures.
- **Typed SDK structs** `model.MediationProfile` and `model.MediationDecision`, and the rules `validate.DeclaredOutcomeRule`, `validate.UnavailableMediatorRule`, `validate.AttributeProvenanceRule`, and `validate.RepeatedSubmissionRule`.

### Why it is in the core rather than in a binding

`CHR-SEC-004` already requires that untrusted instructions and retrieved content not expand an actor's authority. A mediation point is where that requirement is enforced, so `CHR-MED-007` states the general rule: an attribute asserted by the mediated runtime, the client, or the submitted material may tighten a constraint but never relax one. Only the wire format belongs to a binding; the model does not.

The chapter defines no transport, payload encoding, authentication scheme, or detection technique, consistent with the scope in the overview. A platform interface offering only allow and deny is a conforming binding of a profile declaring only those outcomes; a profile declaring `modify` cannot be bound to it (`CHR-BIND-002`).

### Migration

Every document must declare `"charterSpecVersion": "1.1.0"`; documents are otherwise unchanged, and no existing kind, rule, or requirement changed meaning. Implementations that do not mediate acts need no `MediationProfile` and remain conforming: the new rules find nothing to check when no mediation documents exist.

Conformance claims regenerate against the 1.1.0 manifest; the core-model profile now lists 24 rules. Re-run `charter claim` for each active profile.

migrations.title: Definitions declare the version their instances name
migrations.summary: AgentDefinition, Task and BusinessProcess now declare their own version, and admission and task-context resolution refuse an instance whose named version the definition does not declare. Until now the version lived only on the referencing document, so an edited definition passed unnoticed — the gap CHR-PROC-005 and CHR-AGENT-006 already forbid. Schema catalogue 2.0.0; the specification is unchanged at 1.0.0.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Breaking — three document kinds gain a required property

| Kind | New required property | Verified against |
|---|---|---|
| `AgentDefinition` | `definitionVersion` | `AgentRuntime.definitionVersion` |
| `Task` | `taskDefinitionVersion` | `TaskInstance.taskDefinitionVersion` |
| `BusinessProcess` | `processDefinitionVersion` | `ProcessInstance.processDefinitionVersion` |

Every existing document of these kinds must declare the version its instances already name; validation rejects it otherwise.

### Why

`CapabilityContract` already closes this loop — `VersionPolicy.Compatible(required, offered)` reads the offered version off the contract document. The three definition kinds did not: the version lived only on the runtime or instance pointing at them, so two assertions from the same side were compared to each other. Editing a definition in place left both saying `"1"` and admission passed against changed content — exactly what **CHR-PROC-005** ("execution state MUST NOT silently modify the normative definition") and **CHR-AGENT-006** (attribution to the runtime that performed it) forbid. No new requirement: the schema simply made the existing ones uncheckable.

### Enforcement

- `agent.BaseAdmission.Admit` refuses when `def.DefinitionVersion != rt.DefinitionVersion` (CHR-AGENT-006).
- `process.BaseContextResolver.TaskContext` returns `ErrDefinition` when a task or process instance names a version its definition does not declare.

### Migration

Add the property to each definition document, matching what its instances name. Implementations that mint definitions must set it, and must issue a new version — not an in-place edit — when a definition changes.

migrations.title: Keel 1.2.64 compatibility and fenced ledger claims
migrations.summary: Updates the optional Keel adapter from keel v1.2.62 to v1.2.64 and replaces adapter-local code with the primitives keel upstreamed: the caller session, the fenced idempotency ledger, and the query side of the table logger. `capability.Ledger` adopts the fence. The Charter specification, schema catalogue, conformance profiles, and document formats are unchanged from 1.0.0.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Versions

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`, `x-charter-schema-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.0.4 |
| Optional keel adapter (`sdk/adapter/keel`) | keel v1.2.64 |

## Compatibility impact

The normative Charter contract and all document formats remain compatible with 1.0.0. Source-level migrations:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `Session`, `SessionFromContext`, `Session.HasScope` | `common.CallerSession`, `common.CallerSessionFromContext`, `CallerSession.HasScope` |
| adapter `ErrUnauthenticated` | `common.ErrUnauthenticated`; `common.ErrCallerIdentityConflict` is also refused with 401 at the gate |
| `JobContext(ctx, principal, partnerID, requestID)` | `common.WithCallerSession(ctx, common.CallerSession{Principal: principal, PartnerID: partnerID, RequestID: requestID})` |
| `IdentityMap.Actor(ctx, Session)`, `Caller.Actor` result, `Clearance.Session` | `common.CallerSession` in each place |
| `TableLogStore.Logger port.TableLogger` | `TableLogStore.Logger ChangeLog` (`port.TableLogger` plus `port.ChangeQuerier`); keel's write-only file logger no longer compiles as a store |
| `capability.Ledger.Complete(ctx, key, result)`, `Release(ctx, key)`, `MarkUnknown(ctx, key)` | each takes the `fence` that `Begin` granted in `LedgerEntry.Fence`; `BaseMemoryLedger` refuses a missing or stale fence with `ErrLedgerFence` and any change to a completed entry with `ErrLedgerTransition` |
| reconciling an unknown outcome by key alone | present `capability.Result.LedgerFence`, which only an unreconciled unknown outcome carries; executed, replayed, and released results clear it |
| a downstream `capability.Ledger` over its own table | `keeladapter.Ledger{Keel: idempotency.NewPgsqlLedger(db, 0)}` or `idempotency.MemoryLedger`, with keel's `idempotency` schema module installed |

## Adoption

1. Upgrade with `go get github.com/nauticana/charter@v1.0.4` and, when using `sdk/adapter/keel`, keel v1.2.64.
2. Replace the removed session symbols and `JobContext` with their `common` counterparts; a custom `IdentityMap` changes only its `Actor` parameter type.
3. Give `TableLogStore` a logger that answers `FindChanges`.
4. Thread the fence through custom `capability.Ledger` implementations and reconciliation tooling, or compose the adapter `Ledger` over keel's ledger with a zero lease.
5. Run the downstream test suite. No Charter documents, schemas, fixtures, or conformance claims require migration.

migrations.title: Tenant-scoped agent principals and delegation chains
migrations.summary: Corrects the built-in Keel agent-principal shape to carry the authenticated tenant required by Scout's grant source, defines the stable agent identifier contract, and adds a delegation-chain carrier to governed invocations and authority requests. The Charter specification, schema catalogue, and conformance profiles are unchanged from 1.0.0.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Versions

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`, `x-charter-schema-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.0.3 |
| Optional keel adapter (`sdk/adapter/keel`) | keel v1.2.62 |

## Agent principal contract

Version 1.0.2 emitted an agent principal with no scope. A keel `GrantSource` registered with the required `tenant_id` filter therefore failed closed on scope arity. `BaseClaimIdentityMap.Principal` now emits `model.Principal{Kind: AgentPrincipalKind, ID: actor.ID, Scope: []any{session.PartnerID}}` and refuses an agent session without a positive partner/tenant id.

A downstream agent grant source conforms to this contract:

| Grant source field | Required value |
|---|---|
| Kind | `keeladapter.AgentPrincipalKind` |
| Subject column | `agent_id` |
| Subject value | exact stable Charter `AgentIdentity` id |
| Filters | `[]string{"tenant_id"}` |
| Scope value | authenticated keel `Session.PartnerID` |

Downstreams should reference `AgentPrincipalKind` rather than hardcode `"agent"`. The grant table and its registration remain downstream-owned.

## Delegation chain

`model.AuthorityChain` and `model.AuthorityHop` carry a verified acting path, ordered immediate delegator first and original authority last like the RFC 8693 nested `act` claim. Each hop carries its grant reference, delegator, remaining depth, `Limit` bounds, `Validity`, and approval requirement; it never carries a credential.

`capability.Invocation`, `authority.Request`, and `authority.ApprovalRequest` now carry `AuthorityChain`. `AbstractInvoker` threads it into authority and approval evaluation, invokes the approval gate when any hop requires approval, and includes each delegator's performed actions in separation-of-duties evaluation. `DelegationPolicy.Check` fails closed on malformed references, negative or widening depth, ineffective validity, and exceeded typed limits. Authenticity, revocation, and resolution against stored delegation grants remain the responsibility of the downstream verifier that accepts the presented chain before constructing the invocation. Empty chains retain direct-actor behavior.

## Adoption

1. Upgrade with `go get github.com/nauticana/charter@v1.0.3`.
2. Register the keel agent grant source with `AgentPrincipalKind`, subject `agent_id`, and sole filter `tenant_id`; store the exact Charter `AgentIdentity` id in that subject column.
3. Map a verified platform authority path into `model.AuthorityChain` on `capability.Invocation`. Map budget and other bounds to `model.Limit`, dates to `model.Validity`, and per-hop approval bounds to `ApprovalRequired`.
4. Keep verifying grant existence, integrity, and revocation in the platform before invoking Charter. No Charter documents, schemas, fixtures, or conformance claims require migration.

migrations.title: Principal-aware Keel permission gate
migrations.summary: Corrects the optional Keel adapter's permission interface for keel v1.2.62 and passes principal-aware grant subjects through `PermissionGate`. Agent actors can now be authorized directly against a keel `agent` grant source instead of requiring a synthetic user mapping. The Charter specification, schema catalogue, and conformance profiles are unchanged from 1.0.0.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Versions

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`, `x-charter-schema-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.0.2 |
| Optional keel adapter (`sdk/adapter/keel`) | keel v1.2.62 |

## Compatibility impact

The normative Charter contract and all document formats remain compatible with 1.0.0. Version 1.0.1 updated the token identity type but left Charter's local `PermissionChecker` on keel's old user-id signature. That interface compiled in isolation, but `port.DatabaseRepository` no longer satisfied it. Version 1.0.2 corrects the adapter contract:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `PermissionChecker.CheckActionPermission(ctx, userID int, ...)` | `PermissionChecker.CheckActionPermission(ctx, principal model.Principal, ...)` |
| `IdentityMap.UserID(ctx, actor)` | `IdentityMap.Principal(ctx, actor)` |

`PermissionGate` now passes the grant-evaluation `model.Principal` to `CheckActionPermission`, and a compile-time assertion verifies that `port.DatabaseRepository` satisfies `PermissionChecker`.

`BaseClaimIdentityMap` maps a human actor to `model.UserPrincipal` using its `keel_user_id` claim. It maps an agent actor directly to `model.Principal{Kind: "agent", ID: actor.ID}`; an agent token no longer needs a `keel_user_id` claim. Register the corresponding `agent` grant source in keel before repository initialization. If that source declares extra filters, provide a custom `IdentityMap` that returns their values in `Principal.Scope` in registration order. Charter's authority model remains platform-neutral and unchanged.

## Adoption

1. Upgrade with `go get github.com/nauticana/charter@v1.0.2`.
2. Update custom `PermissionChecker` implementations to accept `model.Principal`, and replace custom `IdentityMap.UserID` methods with `Principal`.
3. For human actors, return `model.UserPrincipal(userID)`. For agent actors, register a keel `agent` grant source and return its principal kind, stable id, and any configured scope values.
4. Wire `PermissionGate.Keel` directly to a keel v1.2.62 `port.DatabaseRepository` implementation and run the downstream test suite. No Charter documents, schemas, fixtures, or conformance claims require migration.

migrations.title: Keel 1.2.62 compatibility
migrations.summary: Updates the optional Keel adapter from keel v1.2.61 to v1.2.62 and adopts Keel's renamed OAuth token identity type. The Charter specification, schema catalogue, conformance profiles, and runtime behavior are unchanged from 1.0.0.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Versions

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`, `x-charter-schema-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.0.1 |
| Optional keel adapter (`sdk/adapter/keel`) | keel v1.2.62 |

## Compatibility impact

The normative Charter contract and all document formats remain compatible with 1.0.0. The optional Go adapter has one source-level migration caused by keel v1.2.62 moving OAuth token identity out of its interface-only `port` package:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `*port.Principal` | `*model.TokenPrincipal` |
| `Session.Principal *port.Principal` | `Session.Principal *model.TokenPrincipal` |
| `JobContext(ctx, *port.Principal, ...)` | `JobContext(ctx, *model.TokenPrincipal, ...)` |

This token identity is distinct from keel's new `model.Principal`, which represents the subject of a database grant decision. Charter's authority model remains platform-neutral and is unchanged.

## Adoption

1. Upgrade with `go get github.com/nauticana/charter@v1.0.1`.
2. If using `sdk/adapter/keel`, upgrade keel to v1.2.62.
3. Replace constructed or referenced `port.Principal` values with `model.TokenPrincipal`; update imports from `github.com/nauticana/keel/port` to `github.com/nauticana/keel/model` where the token principal was the only port symbol used.
4. Run the downstream test suite. No Charter documents, schemas, fixtures, or conformance claims require migration.

migrations.summary: First released version of the Charter specification (12 chapters, 111 requirements), the 40-kind schema catalogue with three conformance format schemas, the conformance corpus (core-model: 20 semantic rules; agent-runtime: 8 and system-adapter: 4 runtime-behavioral rules; 45 fixtures), the Go reference SDK, the charter CLI, and the optional keel adapter.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Versions

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`, `x-charter-schema-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.0.0 |
| Optional keel adapter (`sdk/adapter/keel`) | keel v1.2.55 |

## Compatibility impact

None: this is the first release. Documents written against the unreleased `draft` version must set `charterSpecVersion` to `1.0.0`; `charter validate` rejects any other value. Action records must carry the `disposition` introduced with CHR-EVID-010.

## Conformance

All 45 manifest fixtures pass; the reference SDK's claims for the three active profiles are committed under `conformance/claims/` and regenerated by `charter claim` on every release. Per CHR-CONF-010, later minor and patch releases keep these fixtures runnable.

## Adoption

1. `go get github.com/nauticana/charter@v1.0.0`.
2. Validate documents with `charter validate -conformance conformance <dir>`.
3. Runtimes implement `validate.Subject`, adapters `validate.AdapterSubject`, and claim a profile with `charter claim`.
